subject: Negotiating breach notification timelines & cooperation language
messages:
From: Susan Park <susan.dpo@atlashealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@atlashealth.com
Date: 2026-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on breach notification timing and cooperation scope

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recent SIG and SOC2 excerpts — helpful. As we move toward finalizing the data processing addendum, our legal team needs clarity on two items related to incident response:

1) Notification timeline: our DPA template requires the processor to notify the controller "without undue delay and in any case within 72 hours of becoming aware." Given Redwood's hosted/dedicated/private modes, can you confirm whether you are able to commit to that 72-hour maximum, or if you require additional latitude (e.g., confirming scope before notification)?

2) Cooperation & evidence: if we request forensic evidence (logs, packet captures, root-cause analysis) to support regulatory reporting or our DPIA, what is your operational SLT for delivering initial evidence packets and subsequent updates? Also, would Redwood allow an independent forensic firm to conduct analysis under an NDA if we request it?

I've attached a short SIG checklist showing the items we'd expect in an incident package. Please loop in your legal/ops folks and let us know the standard language you prefer for the DPA incident section.

Thanks,
Susan Park
Data Protection Officer
Atlas Health
[attachment: Atlas-SIG-Checklist.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Park <susan.dpo@atlashealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-20T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on breach notification timing and cooperation scope

Hi Susan — appreciate the clear asks. Looping in Laura (legal) and Rafael (infrastructure ops) to propose Redwood's standard positions. High level: we aim to balance prompt controller notification with preserving forensic integrity.

Short answers up front:
- Notification: Redwood proposes initial notification "without undue delay and no later than 72 hours after we confirm a security incident affecting customer data." We typically avoid absolute commitments that require notification before we can confirm scope (to avoid false positives).
- Evidence & forensics: we can provide initial log bundles within 3 business days of confirmation and substantive updates within 5 business days; final post-incident reports typically within 30 calendar days. We will consider independent forensics under NDA and with mutually agreed scope.

I'm attaching a redline of the DPA incident section with the above language as a starting point. Laura — can you review and tighten the wording on exceptions (law enforcement, national security) and any indemnity/fee language around third-party forensics? Rafael — can you confirm typical log preservation windows and whether we can make 12-month accruals available on request?

Next step: if that framing is acceptable to Atlas, we can propose a short call to resolve exact wording and rates for extended preservation or third-party forensic access.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Director, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0143
[attachment: draft-DPA-redlines.docx]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Susan Park <susan.dpo@atlashealth.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-20T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on breach notification timing and cooperation scope

Susan / Marissa — quick legal suggestions to reduce ambiguity:

1) Timeline: propose this text for the DPA incident clause: "Processor shall notify Controller without undue delay and, in any event, within forty-eight (48) hours of becoming aware of a confirmed security incident that reasonably appears to affect Controller's data. An 'awareness' includes receipt of information from monitoring or a credible external report. If initial notification occurs before root cause is established, Processor shall include a statement of known facts and a plan for substantive updates."

2) Updates & final report: "Processor will provide substantive updates no later than five (5) business days after the initial notice and a final incident report within thirty (30) calendar days, unless a longer timeline is reasonably required."

3) Cooperation: limit request scope to "access to logs, anonymized/pseudonymized data, and summaries of impacted systems." For independent forensics: allow with prior written consent from Processor, an NDA, and at Client's expense. Also include preservation obligations (see below).

4) Preservation & retention: propose a preservation baseline of 30 days for hot logs; for regulatory or litigation needs, Controller may request extended preservation up to twelve (12) months, subject to reasonable fees. Exceptions for law enforcement requests and national security disclosures should be explicitly recognized.

I'll attach a proposed incident clause; Marissa, please confirm if the 48-hour initial timeline is operationally acceptable or if it is better to stick with 72 hours as your initial message suggested.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
[attachment: proposed-incident-clause.docx]

From: Susan Park <susan.dpo@atlashealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, legal@atlashealth.com
Date: 2026-05-20T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on breach notification timing and cooperation scope

Thanks Laura — very helpful. A couple of points from Atlas's perspective:

- 48 hours would be ideal for initial notification from a controller compliance standpoint but 72 hours is acceptable if Redwood needs that window to confirm. Would you consider a hybrid: "initial notification as soon as practicable and no later than 72 hours," with a commitment to follow-up within 48 hours if new facts emerge?

- Preservation: we prefer a 12-month preservation guarantee for logs relevant to an incident; if that is a fees-based add-on that is fine, but please state the process and lead time to request it.

- Independent forensics: Atlas requires the ability to retain a third-party forensic specialist in certain high-risk incidents (e.g., PHI exfiltration). We'll accept an NDA and a mutually agreed scope; Redwood's requirement for prior written consent is acceptable so long as consent is not unreasonably withheld.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to nail these points and confirm any commercial terms for extended preservation?

Best,
Susan

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Park <susan.dpo@atlashealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-21T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on breach notification timing and cooperation scope

Susan — quick ops note on feasibility:

- Hot logs: default retention in our hosted clusters is 30 days. We can do a 12-month preservation hold on a per-incident basis, but it requires a request from the customer's security contact and may incur storage/-processing fees. Lead time to enable extended preservation for an incident we just detected is immediate (we can snapshot and copy to cold storage within 24 hours), but longer-term indexing and analysis export may take 48–72 hours.

- Evidence delivery: initial log bundles and a timeline summary: target 3 business days after confirmation. Larger exports (pcap, full KV caches) will take longer depending on scope. Independent forensics — we will require an NDA and reasonable coordinate windows; we will not unreasonably withhold access but need to protect other customers and system integrity.

I'll prepare a short ops appendix we can attach to the DPA that lays out preservation actions, evidence formats, and pricing for extended holds.

--
Rafael Mendes
VP, Infrastructure Operations | Redwood Inference
